name: cisco-pt-mcp

tools.name: addDevice
tools.description: Add a network device to the workspace. Call getNetwork first if unsure whether the chosen deviceName is already taken; names must be unique.

deviceName.description: Unique name for the device (must not already exist).

deviceModel.description: Device model. Router: 2911/1941/2811/2901. Switch: 2960-24TT/2950-24/3560-24PS. End device: PC-PT/Server-PT/Laptop-PT/Printer-PT.

tools.name: addModule
tools.description: Add an interface module to a device. Powers the device off, installs the module, powers it back on.

tools.name: addLink
tools.description: Connect two devices with a cable. Both interfaces must be free (in_use=false in getNetwork output). If unsure, call getNetwork first.

linkType.description: Cable type. Use 'straight' for most LAN, 'cross' for PC-PC, 'serial' for WAN.

tools.name: removeDevice
tools.description: Remove one or more devices from the workspace.

deviceNames.description: Array of existing device names to remove.

tools.name: removeLink
tools.description: Remove one or more cables. Each entry identifies one endpoint of the link.

tools.name: configurePcIp
tools.description: Configure IP settings on a PC or end device.

dhcpEnabled.description: True for DHCP, false for static IP.

tools.name: configureIosDevice
tools.description: Execute IOS commands on a router or switch. Commands run from global config and are saved with 'write memory'.

tools.name: getNetwork
tools.description: Snapshot of the entire workspace: every device, its interfaces (with in_use flags), and every cable. Call this before addLink or removeDevice when unsure of current state.

tools.name: getDeviceInfo
tools.description: Detailed info about one device, including interfaces and incident links.

tools.name: setSimulationMode
tools.description: Switch Packet Tracer between simulation mode and realtime mode. Simulation mode is required before sending PDUs or stepping through traffic.

toSimMode.description: true = simulation mode, false = realtime mode.

tools.name: getSimulationStatus
tools.description: Query the current simulation state: mode (realtime or simulation), elapsed simulation time, PDU frame count, and current frame index.

tools.name: stepSimulation
tools.description: Step the simulation forward or backward, or reset it entirely. PT must already be in simulation mode (use setSimulationMode first).

direction.description: 'forward' advances one step, 'backward' goes back one step, 'reset' clears all PDUs and returns to time 0.

steps.description: Number of steps to take (ignored for 'reset'). Defaults to 1.

tools.name: sendPdu
tools.description: Add an ICMP ping PDU between two devices using PT's native Simple PDU mechanism. Automatically enables simulation mode if not already active. Use stepSimulation to advance and getPduResults to check if the ping succeeded.

tools.name: renameDevice
tools.description: Rename an existing device. The new name must be unique in the workspace.

newName.description: New unique name for the device.

tools.name: moveDevice
tools.description: Move a device to new coordinates on the logical workspace canvas.

tools.name: setPower
tools.description: Power a device on or off.

power.description: true = power on, false = power off.

tools.name: getPduResults
tools.description: Read the outcome of PDUs in the current simulation — source, destination, traffic type, and status (accepted/dropped/in_transit/etc). Call after stepSimulation to verify connectivity. Use the types filter to show only ICMP, TCP, etc. and hide STP/DTP background noise.

types.description: Only return frames matching these traffic type names (e.g. ["ICMP"], ["ICMP","ARP"]). Omit to return all frames.

tools.name: getCommandLog
tools.description: Read the IOS command history logged by Packet Tracer. Optionally filter by device name and cap the number of returned entries.

deviceName.description: Return only entries from this device. Omit to return all devices.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return, newest first. Defaults to 50.
